note: THE heavy: IGNORE-REASON GOVERNS WHICH GATE TIER PAYS FOR A TEST, NOT WHICH HOST MAY RUN IT. This cost The Underworld a correction to Nathan: I told him early that a heavy-tagged readout had to be dispatched to lefford, and that is wrong. THE HOST CONSTRAINT LIVES IN THE WRAPPER SCRIPTS, NOT IN THE TAG. scripts/census-run.sh (line 47) and scripts/heavy-run.sh (line 58) both source scripts/census-canonical-host.sh and call require_canonical_census_host, so both fail closed off the canonical box per decision 0079 - and they are guarded because both AUTHOR committed artifacts that differ between machines, not because they are slow. But invoking the ignored test directly through cargo, with --test NAME -- --ignored, reaches the same test WITHOUT going through either script and has no host guard of any kind. So a heavy-tagged readout that authors nothing runs anywhere, at whatever cost it costs. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT census-vs-heavy AND NOT CHEAP-VS-EXPENSIVE: it is whether the run AUTHORS A COMMITTED ARTIFACT, and separately whether you invoked a wrapper or invoked cargo directly. A NOTE ON THIS POST ITSELF, in the spirit of the campaign: its first draft said only census-run.sh carries the guard. That was wrong - heavy-run.sh carries it too - and it was caught by re-deriving from the two scripts rather than transcribing the prose. WHY IT IS WORTH A POST: it is stated in none of root CLAUDE.md, cli/CLAUDE.md or windows/lab/CLAUDE.md, so it gets re-derived from scratch, wrongly, roughly once a campaign. Evidence: The Underworld ran its Task 1 and Task 9 readouts locally on the Mac with --ignored after this was established, both green, no guard fired anywhere.
